title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
description: Ten distinct Johns Hopkins study environments, from silent reading rooms and reservable collaboration spaces to residential and medical-campus options.

cards.title: Settle Into Brody’s Quietest Room
cards.subtitle: Silent individual study inside Brody Learning Commons
cards.notes: Bring focused, silent work and choose a seat in the dedicated reading room; use the atrium or group rooms when conversation is necessary.
cards.short_summary: A purpose-built quiet room for distraction-light individual work.
cards.evidence_claim: Sheridan Libraries identifies Brody’s Quiet Reading Room as a silent study area and distinguishes it from collaborative spaces in the atrium and group rooms.
cards.access_notes: Located inside Brody Learning Commons; a J-card is required for the building. Check the live library-hours page before visiting.

cards.title: Book a Brody Group Room
cards.subtitle: Reservable rooms with whiteboards and presentation equipment
cards.notes: Reserve through 25Live for collaborative work, arrive within ten minutes of the start time, and keep the session within the posted booking limits.
cards.short_summary: A reservable collaboration setup for projects that need discussion and shared displays.
cards.evidence_claim: Sheridan Libraries provides reservable group study rooms in Brody; student bookings are limited to two hours daily and reservations take priority over walk-ins.
cards.access_notes: JHU students may reserve within a rolling 48-hour window. J-card entry is required, and only Hopkins affiliates may enter library buildings.

cards.title: Choose Your Pace at the Annex
cards.subtitle: Quiet rooms, collaborative areas, carrels, and outdoor tables
cards.notes: Match the room to the assignment: take a carrel for solo reading, use a collaborative area for discussion, or move to the garden furniture outside.
cards.short_summary: A house-like library annex offering several study modes in one destination.
cards.evidence_claim: Sheridan Libraries says the MSE Library Annex offers quiet rooms with individual carrels, collaborative areas, outdoor furniture, printing, and core library services.
cards.access_notes: The Annex is a Homewood study space requiring a J-card. Consult the live locations-and-hours page because daily access changes by term.

cards.title: Read Under Gilman’s High Ceiling
cards.subtitle: The 24-hour Homewood reading room known as “The Hut”
cards.notes: Use the carrels or large tables for quiet work, keep conversations elsewhere, and carry your J-card for evening entry to Gilman Hall.
cards.short_summary: A formal Gilman Hall reading room equipped for sustained quiet study.
cards.evidence_claim: Sheridan Libraries lists the Hutzler Reading Room as a 24-hour study space and describes carrels, large tables, desks, sofas, printing, copying, and scanning.
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours according to the current library listing; J-card access is required after 6 p.m. The specialized Hut South area is limited to designated graduate students.

cards.title: Take the First-Floor Reading Room
cards.subtitle: A dedicated room amid Hodson Hall’s multi-floor study seating
cards.notes: Start in the first-floor reading room for concentrated work; move to the lobby carrels and tables if you need a more open setting.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated reading room supported by additional seating throughout Hodson Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Sheridan Libraries identifies a reading room on Hodson Hall’s first floor, plus library carrels, tables, and seating in lobby areas on all three floors.
cards.access_notes: The current library listing identifies Hodson Hall as a study space and requires J-card access after 6 p.m.; verify live hours before arrival.

cards.title: Study Beneath Peabody’s Stacks
cards.subtitle: Quiet study at Johns Hopkins’ Peabody campus library
cards.notes: Plan a quiet reading session around the library’s posted schedule, and check closure notices before taking the shuttle from Homewood.
cards.short_summary: A visually distinctive historic library that Sheridan Libraries designates for quiet study.
cards.evidence_claim: Sheridan Libraries identifies George Peabody Library as a study space and describes it as a destination for quiet study on the Peabody campus.
cards.access_notes: Hours and closures vary and are posted on the live library-hours page; confirm the library is open before traveling to the Peabody campus.

cards.title: Keep It Silent in Welch West
cards.subtitle: Silent study on the second floor of Welch Medical Library
cards.notes: Choose this reading room for work that benefits from silence, display your JH ID at entry, and redirect group discussion to the East Reading Room.
cards.short_summary: The designated silent-study half of Welch Library’s paired reading rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Welch Medical Library identifies the West Reading Room as a silent study area on the second floor of the Welch Library Building.
cards.source_title: Where do I find study spaces?
cards.access_notes: A JH ID must be worn and displayed when entering Welch Library; visitors must check in with security. Building hours are posted online.

cards.title: Work Together in Welch East
cards.subtitle: Group and open study on Welch Library’s second floor
cards.notes: Use the open layout for collaborative coursework and conversation, then shift to the West Reading Room when the task calls for silence.
cards.short_summary: Welch Library’s designated option for open and group-oriented study.
cards.evidence_claim: Welch Medical Library identifies the East Reading Room as a group and open-space study area on the building’s second floor.
cards.source_title: Where do I find study spaces?
cards.access_notes: A JH ID must be worn and displayed when entering Welch Library; visitors must check in with security. Confirm current building hours online.

cards.title: Claim a Powered Bayview Carrel
cards.subtitle: Four research carrels and a reservable conference room
cards.notes: Request the access code before visiting, use a powered carrel for solo research, or reserve the conference room for a screen-sharing session.
cards.short_summary: A clinical-research study room with powered carrels and presentation capability.
cards.evidence_claim: Welch at Bayview provides four powered study carrels, three desktop computers, and a conference room with a monitor and HDMI connection.
cards.access_notes: A requested code is required for 24/7 access. Conference-room reservations are limited to two hours daily and may be made up to 21 days ahead.

cards.title: Use the Winter Library Around the Clock
cards.subtitle: A compact 24-hour study room in Scott-Bates Commons
cards.notes: Enter from 33rd Street if you do not live in the building, bring your J-card, and use the ten-seat room for a small-scale study session.
cards.short_summary: A compact residential-campus library explicitly opened to all Johns Hopkins students.
cards.evidence_claim: Johns Hopkins’ 2026 Homewood study-space listing identifies the ten-seat Winter Library in Scott-Bates Commons as open 24/7 and available to all students.
cards.access_notes: The official listing says the room is open 24/7 to all students; non-residential students should use the building’s 33rd Street entrance.
